pairs.question: cum saepius duplicaret numerum dierum, cur ita faceret?
pairs.answer: Quia, quanto diutius considero, tanto mihi spes videtur obscurior.
pairs.derivation: Hiero/Simonides anecdote within Cotta's speech. The interrogative is Hiero's reported question 'requireret, cur ita faceret'; dropped the asking-narration 'admiransque Hiero requireret' (framing of the asking) but kept the verbatim setup 'cum saepius duplicaret numerum dierum' so 'ita faceret' has a referent (Simonides repeatedly doubling the days he asks for). The answer is Simonides' verbatim direct reply, with the framing tag 'inquit' (which interrupts it: 'Quia, quanto diutius considero,' inquit 'tanto...') removed and the two quoted halves rejoined contiguously as the speaker's own utterance; ends at the full stop. It genuinely answers the 'why'.
